title: The Phase 6 per-user loss bound (ERC4626_MAX_LOSS_BPS = 2) sits inside autoDOLA's stepwise live spread, so :preview's go/no-go flips between blocks. The bound is enforced only in forge's local pass, so a regime step during the Ledger session lands a migration above 2 bps that only :verify's live-balance aggregate detects
description: `ERC4626_MAX_LOSS_BPS = 2` bounds each migrating user's full round trip (V1 exit plus V2 re-deposit) on the autoDOLA and autoUSDC pools. Its NatSpec (L147-153) justifies 2 bps as '~2.3x the worst observation' from a single planning-block sample (autoDOLA 0.034 bps round trip), 'loose enough not to trip on the autopools' own valuation spread'. The fork shows otherwise. autoDOLA's deposit and redeem spread is symmetric per leg and moves in discrete, state-driven steps: 0.017 bps per leg at 25981150, stepping up at block 25981232 (tx 0xbcca6e62…) to 1.035 bps per leg (2.07 bps round trip) for ~6,769 blocks (~22.5 h), then down at 25988001 to 0.474 bps per leg. Story 087's FOR-THE-HUMAN note treats this as a static 'cannot broadcast today' condition. The condition is not static. At 25985945 the real preview reverts in Phase 6 (all 9 DOLA users at 2.069-2.093 bps). At 25988932 the same preview passes all phases and all nine GLOBAL_PAUSE stages (worst DOLA user 0.959 bps). The operator-visible consequence is not obvious. Every `require` in the script, including this bound, runs only in forge's local pass before any transaction is sent. A green :preview or a green local pass therefore bounds nothing about the Phase 6 transactions that land ~30 Ledger-signed transactions later. If a spread step lands in that window, the migration executes on chain above the stated 2 bps. Afterwards: (a) a resume or preview re-run passes, because the per-user loop is empty on a resume leg and the exit-realization bound only sees the 1.035 bps exit leg; (b) :verify's per-user credit→credited check (1.058 bps) and realization bound also pass; (c) only the per-pool aggregate on live `V2.totalStaked` reverts, by 0.008936 DOLA. Because that aggregate reads a live balance, it goes permanently red, and the `&& :preview` smoke tail never runs. By inspection (not fork-tested), about 0.009 DOLA of organic V2 stake would turn it green again. Story 087's Concerns claim that 'the per-user in-leg check and the verifier's per-user credit check still bound the total'. For the verifier this does not hold: its per-user check covers only the re-deposit leg.
impact: Operational and spec-drift (story 082/083 per-user bound ≤ 2 bps + 1000 wei). Today the preview-based go/no-go is non-deterministic across autopool regime steps: an operator who read story 087's 'cannot broadcast' note sees a green preview now, and may later hit a local-pass revert (fail-closed, zero transactions sent). By inspection (not executed: S L484/L516/L649 call `_writeProgress` during the local pass, as the //:broadcast RESUME note documents), that revert still leaves phantom addresses in progress.stable-staker-v2-cutover.1.json, which the next run refuses until the file is trimmed. The rarer case is an in-session step that lands a >2 bps migration. The only detector is a live-balance aggregate that stays red until organic stakes mask it. Value at stake is negligible at current pool sizes (2.09 bps of ~1,222 DOLA ≈ 0.26 DOLA per full round trip; the overshoot beyond the spec is ~0.009 DOLA). No asset theft and no non-resumable brick. Hence Low.
lawAnalysis: Law 3: leaving the constant untuned is a KNOWING owner deferral recorded in story 087 and is not reported as such. The non-obvious parts are in scope as a footgun: the go/no-go flips (not a static 'too tight'); a local-pass pass is not an on-chain bound; the stated NatSpec rationale is empirically false; and the verifier's per-user check does not bound the total, contrary to the story's Concerns. Distinct from F-02 436848b0 (wont-fix: who bears the loss) — this is about gate calibration and enforcement point, not loss allocation.
evidence: side-effects.json autoDolaSpreadRegime + harnessResults: fork-logs/preview-25988932.log (PASS, 9 stages); fork-logs/r34-test_B.log (test_B_previewRun_atStory087Block: run() REVERTED 'cutover-post: cutover lost more principal than the strategy can explain'; test_B_liveLoss_* at 25981150 / 25985945 / 25988932); fork-logs/r34-test_B_driftLanding.log (resume-shape PASS, verifier REVERTED 'verify: aggregate: V2 booked total 1222474121170267702467 below the principal due net of self-exits (floor 1222483056933011775952) for DOLA'). Fork-confirmed.
recommendation: 1) Re-derive ERC4626_MAX_LOSS_BPS in its own story from a multi-day sample of autoDOLA/autoUSDC previewRedeem/previewDeposit versus convertToAssets, covering at least one up-step (observed max 2.07 bps round trip), for example 2x the observed max (~5 bps). Rewrite the L147-153 NatSpec to cite that sample. 2) In `_initiatePool`, for ERC4626 pools, pre-quote the round trip before `initiateMigration`, as already done for the market strategy: exit = previewRedeem(convertToShares(P)), re-deposit = convertToAssets(previewDeposit(credit)). Log `LOSS_HEADROOM|token|bps` in preview and STOP AND REPORT when it exceeds the bound, so the operator sees the margin, not just pass/fail. 3) Runbook (//:broadcast): state that the Phase 6 bound depends on the autopool regime, that :preview must be re-run immediately before signing, and that a :verify aggregate red immediately after a green local pass means the regime moved mid-session (resume will not detect it). Also state what to do with a progress file left by a local-pass revert: delete it when no transaction was sent. 4) Correct story 087's Concerns claim about the verifier's per-user check bounding the total, or add a per-user total (pre → credited) check to the verifier reconstructing each user's pre-migration principal from the MigratedOut credit as credit·P/min(R,P).
